card.name: Adverse-event nouns before 'reported' or 'sometimes'
card.fires_on: The last word or word part of a named adverse condition in a warnings section, such as 'necrosis', 'symptom complex' or 'fractures have'. The next words are usually 'and other', 'sometimes referred to as' or 'been reported'.

modes.label: Ends of condition names
modes.description: The final part of a long medical condition name in a warnings heading or sentence.
modes.example: Long-term administration of NSAIDs has resulted in renal papillary nec<<rosis>> and other renal injury.

modes.label: Condition noun or verb before 'reported'
modes.description: A condition name or the verb right after it, just before text saying it has been reported.
modes.example: Atypical subtrochanteric and diaphyseal femoral fractures<< have>> been reported in patients receiving bisphosph

modes.label: Syndrome label
modes.description: The word 'complex' after 'symptom', just before the syndrome is given another name.
modes.example: A potentially fatal symptom<< complex>> sometimes referred to as Neuroleptic M

card.writes: It promotes hedging words such as 'seems', 'presumably' and 'apparently', so the text goes on to qualify or attribute the statement.
card.plain: It fires at the end of a named side effect, just before the label says how it was reported or described.
